WHAT WERE TK'S EARLY POLITICAL VIEWS, IF ANY?

In article <19990404193047.13113.00003418@ng-cg1.aol.com>,
rossgetman@aol.com (RossGetman) wrote:
>...
>Most of Kaczynski's problems
>with his parents with
>Kaczynski in his adolescent years
>and early twenties, I believe, were
>over politics.  And not due to 
>his lack of social skills.

What evidence do we have regarding TK's political views, if any,
during adolescence and his pre-Berkeley twenties?  

Is it just speculation based on the idea that adolescents always
rebel against the politics of their parents?  Or do you have
something more?

By all accounts, TK was a social outcast while he was at Harvard
in the late 1950s and very early 1960s -- pre-Vietnam -- when the
dominant opinion on campus would have been "country-club"
conservative.  Under such circumstances, TK is unlikely to have
acquired conservative or far-right leanings from other students
there -- more likely the opposite would be true and he would have
learned to strongly reject the views they held.

REVOLUTIONARY ROLE MODELS
                                             
There is the intriguing account of TK having dreams at Harvard
about being being a revolutionary leader and exhorting mobs to
revolutionary violence [Johnson report].  Unfortunately, it
wasn't specified which particular revolutionary leaders TK was
dreaming about imitating.  

We know it wasn't the two-bit revolutionaries of the anti-Vietnam
War ear because nobody had even heard of them in the 1958-62
period when TK was a student at Harvard.  

So what revolutionary figures were well-known in that period and
were commonly depicted as making speeches to mobs of followers?  

Maybe there are some suitable candidates from the American
Revolution but none come to mind.  Perhaps an American poster
could help me here if I've overlooked any good candidates.

Castro was very much in the news during the 1950s and fits the
bill nicely.  Lenin and, maybe, Stalin were commonly viewed in
this way.  If memory serves, Mao was a rather shadowy and exotic
figure at the time and hence a less likely candidate.
                          
All of these are definitely on the left and given the political
leanings of the elder Kaczynski's were unlikely to produced much 
conflict in the family if TK showed interest in them.

[Now something Ross has probably been waiting for.     ]

In the 1950s, Mussolini and especially Hitler were commonly
associated with images of speakers rousing mobs to violence which
could arguably be viewed as revolutionary violence.  If TK had
shown any interest in either of these fellows, then the fur would
certainly have flown in the Kaczynski household.   ;-)

On the other hand, TK may not have had any interest in the
politics of any of these revolutionary role models and been only
attracted to the revolutionary images because it allowed him to
fantasize about being powerful, a leader, in control of a mob of
followers, and able to order acts of violence against his
enemies.

DOES TK HATE LEFTISTS OR JUST MODERN LEFTISTS?

TK himself makes a careful distinction between modern leftism and
earlier types of leftism in section 8 of the Manifesto:

   8. Even so, our conception of leftism will remain a good deal less
   clear than we would wish, but there doesn't seem to be any remedy for
   this. All we are trying to do is indicate in a rough and approximate
   way the two psychological tendencies that we believe are the main
   driving force of modern leftism. We by no means claim to be telling
   the WHOLE truth about leftist psychology. Also, our discussion is
   meant to apply to modern leftism only. We leave open the question of
   the extent to which our discussion could be applied to the leftists of
   the 19th and early 20th century.

It is hardly surprising that encountering the modern type of
leftist at Berkeley -- and probably conflicts with them -- should
have given TK a life-long hatred of modern leftism but judging
from the Manifesto he doesn't harbour much animosity towards old
style leftism.

But the politics of the elder Kaczynski's in the 1940s, 1950s,
and early 1960s would certainly have been old style leftism
rather than the modern variety.  

If TK's animosity towards leftists is rooted in early conflicts
with his parents over old style leftism, why does he concentrate
on attacking only modern leftism like he encountered at Berkeley?

He's certainly in disagreement with the regimentation,
collectivism, and worship of industrialization so prominent in
old style leftism. You'd think that if he'd had major conflicts
over this while he was growing up, he'd have more than a few
words to say about what's wrong with old-style leftists.

WHAT PROBABLY HAPPENED

Ross, if you can come up with credible evidence that TK had
strong political views in his late teens and early twenties, I'll
certainly change my mind but until then, I believe the story is
much simpler.

As a child and teenager, TK probably accepted most of his parents
political views.  His social rejection at Harvard probably
strongly reinforced the liberal/leftist ideas about social and
economic class barriers he had already learned from his parents.  
Harvard probably contributed a life-long hatred of the business
and economic elite, as well.

None of this is likely to have created serious political
conflicts with his parents.  Furthermore, I'd guess that while at
Harvard, he still held fairly strong and quite conventional views
about the importance of education, upward mobility, and success
in a career.

What happened as a graduate student at U. of Michigan, I can only
guess at but it was probably a confusing period for TK.  He was
beginning to succeed as a mathematician but he seems to have been
as socially unsuccessful as ever.  Perhaps he expected more
respect from the classes he was now teaching than he was likely
to get students increasingly concerned with the draft and the
escalating Vietnam War.  At a guess, TK probably felt things
weren't going the way they should have.

I believe the turning point for TK's views about politics and
careers came while he was an Assistant Prof. at Berkeley and
perhaps in the previous year or two at U. of Michigan.  
Unpleasant, direct experience with the leftists at Berkeley lead
to his complete rejection of modern leftism, and probably
old-style leftism to a lesser extent.

Arriving at Berkeley, he had reached a major milestone in his
career but what had that success really brought him.  Respect?  
Social confidence?  Dating success?  Wealth?  Happiness?  

Probably none of the above.  The students were in open revolt
against authority including the educational institutions in
which they hid from draft.  Nobody has yet found any friends TK
made at Berkeley and TK was so desperate for a date that he was
placing lonely-heart ads in the local newspaper.  He would have
been getting an above average salary but he'd probably be putting
in 50, 60, or even 70 hour weeks to earn it and he certainly wasn't
enjoying the money.  He was living in a dismal little rental
house -- not much better than student digs -- in the low rent area
of Berkeley.  As for being happy, the fact he quit as soon as his
two year contract expired tells us all we need to know.

If I'm correct, when TK left Berkeley in 1969, he was adrift
without any sort of mental compass.  Both the leftism and the
careerism instilled by his parents had been experienced
first-hand and found wanting.  He still had plenty of personal
likes and dislikes but he had no mental framework -- no ideology
or overall view of the world -- into which he could fit the
separate pieces.  And he lacked a rationalization for abandoning
of his career.

It would be during the period following Berkeley that TK would
have been searching around for new rationalizations and a new
ideology.  If, as Ross suggests, TK flirted with neo-Nazism --
not impossible given his hatred of modern leftism -- then this
would be the time he would have done it rather than in his
adolescence.

As we all know, TK eventually found his new ideology and armed
with those excuses, fled into the woods to get away from the
world in which he could not function, returning occasionally
to post expressions of his hatred.
